introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geology (0555), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FIVE questions: choosing TWO questions from Section A, TWO from Section B and question 7 in Section C. (Note: Question 7 is compulsory.)

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

regles_choix.texte: Question 7 is compulsory: every candidate answers it. In parts (a) and (b), answer EITHER the first version OR the version after OR.

figures.legende: Figure 1. Geological map (grid 15-22 east, 00-05 north) with legend: A conglomerate, B sandstone, C sandy shale, D shale, E limestone, sandy limestone, doleritic intrusion, fault, stream; dashed 400 contour.
Figure 2. Crystal model (a cube drawn as a wire frame).

incertitudes: Aucun corrige officiel : les reponses modeles sont redigees d'apres les notions classiques du programme O Level de Geologie ; a faire relire par un geologue avant mise en avant. Le sujet est une feuille a completer (lignes pointillees) : les lignes ne sont pas reproduites.

Regle de choix : page de garde « Answer FIVE questions: Choosing Two questions from section A, Two from Section B and question 7 in Section C. (Note: Question 7 is compulsory) ». Code : parmi 2 sur 3 pour SECTION A (questions 1 a 3), parmi 2 sur 3 pour SECTION B (questions 4 a 6), et une regle `consigne` pour SECTION C (question 7 obligatoire, avec choix interne entre deux versions de (a) et de (b)). Page de garde lue : ORDINARY LEVEL, GEOLOGY, code 0555, paper 2, JUNE 2026, deux heures et demie, reference GCE26/0555/2/P52.

Question 7 : choix interne. (a) : version carte (i) 3 + (ii) 2 = 5 OU version discordances (i) 2 + (ii) 2 + (iii) 1 = 5 ; (b) : version modele cristallin (i) 2 + (ii) 2 + (iii) 1 = 5 OU version cube (i) 2 + (ii) 1 + (iii) 2 = 5 ; (c) 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 ; (d) 2 + (1 + 1) + 1 = 5 ; total 20, conforme au sujet. Les versions « OR » sont transcrites en questions separees `a-alt` et `b-alt` (points null : le candidat ne traite que l'une des deux versions, le total reste 20 ; meme convention que Philosophy A Level 2026 P3).

Question 7(a) (version carte) : la carte est un dessin a main levee. Lectures NON certifiees : le trait epais vertical a l'est 18 et les autres traits epais sont lus comme des intrusions de dolerite (meme figure que la legende « doleritic intrusion ») ; les lignes fines (une oblique au sud-ouest, une autre en arc a l'est) sont lues comme faille(s) ou cours d'eau, la distinction n'etant pas nette ; les couches en U emboites (D, E, C) sont lues comme un pli plongeant ; la limite pointillee du conglomerat A est lue comme une discordance (le conglomerat repose sur les couches plus anciennes). Plusieurs reponses du jury peuvent etre acceptables.

Question 7(a)(ii) : la legende est lue comme une colonne stratigraphique (le plus recent en haut : conglomerat A ; le plus ancien en bas : calcaire sableux), et le conglomerat A repose en discordance sur les autres couches. Reponse retenue : roche la plus recente = conglomerat (A) ; la plus ancienne = calcaire sableux (sandy limestone). Les intrusions de dolerite recoupent les couches et sont plus jeunes que celles qu'elles traversent ; cela n'est pas repris dans la reponse. A faire verifier.
Question 7(b)(iii) (version modele cristallin) : le candidat doit marquer une arete sur la figure ; le corrige decrit le geste (fleche et mention « edge » sur une des 12 aretes).

Question 7(c) : le sujet imprime « (2 marks) » pour la couleur, « (2 marks) » pour la trace, « (1 mark) » pour la durete du diamant, soit 5. 7(d) : texture 2 marks, mode de formation 1 + 1, usages du granite 1 mark = 5.

Figures : figure 1 (page 7) et figure 2 (page 8) produites avec le skill reproduire-figure-sans-filigrane (regime B_cuit, filtre de niveaux, controle OCR OK, relues a l'oeil) ; les mentions « Figure 1 / Figure 2 » du sujet sont retirees du recadrage (elles sont dans la legende).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Study the map (Figure 1) and answer questions 7(a)(i) and (ii).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geology-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(i) Outline the different geologic structures found on the map. (3 marks)

(ii) Name the oldest and youngest rocks on the map in Figure 1.

Youngest rock:

Oldest rock:

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Geologic structures on the map** (any three):

1. **Unconformity:** the dashed boundary shows the **conglomerate (A)** resting on the older, folded and tilted beds (B, C, D, E): the conglomerate is younger and lies across their edges.
2. **Fold:** the outcrops of D, C and E curve round in nested U-shapes, so the beds are folded (a **plunging fold**).
3. **Igneous intrusions:** the thick black bands are **dolerite dykes (intrusions)** cutting across the sedimentary beds, including the long straight N-S dyke at easting 18.
4. **Fault(s):** a straight thin line crossing the limestone in the south-west is read as a fault (with the ticked fault symbol of the legend).

**(ii)**

- **Youngest rock: Conglomerate (A)**, because it lies unconformably on top of the other beds (and is the top of the sequence in the legend).
- **Oldest rock: Sandy limestone**, the lowest bed in the sequence, which outcrops in the core of the structure in the extreme south-west corner.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**OR**

(a) (i) How are unconformities recognised on geological maps? (2 marks)

(ii) Define the term outlier. (2 marks)

(iii) The ages of rocks on geologic maps can be determined using; (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Recognising unconformities on a map:**

- The outcrop of the **younger rocks cuts across (truncates) the boundaries and strike of the older rocks** below it: the younger formation lies against several different older beds in turn.
- The younger rocks have a **different dip and strike** (they are not parallel to the older beds), and often begin with a **basal conglomerate**.
- Some formations of the older series are **missing** (overstepped) beneath the younger beds.

**(ii) Outlier:** an **outcrop of younger rock completely surrounded by older rock**, left when erosion removed the younger cover around it.

**(iii)** The ages of rocks on geologic maps can be determined using **fossils (index fossils)** and **radiometric dating** (also the principle of superposition and cross-cutting relationships for relative age).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Study the crystal model (Figure 2) and answer questions 7(b)(i), (ii) and (iii).

![fig-2](gce-ol-geology-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_2.png)

(i) Identify the system to which the crystal model belongs. (2 marks)

(ii) State the number of crystal faces present in the crystal model. (2 marks)

(iii) On the crystal model, label the crystal edge. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The model is a **cube**: three equal axes at right angles, all faces square. It belongs to the **cubic (isometric) crystal system**.

**(ii)** The model has **6 crystal faces** (all square and equal: top, bottom, front, back, left and right).

**(iii)** A **crystal edge** is a **straight line where two adjacent crystal faces meet**. A cube has **12 edges**. On the drawing, mark any one of them (for example the front top horizontal line) with an arrow and write the word **"edge"** beside it.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**OR**

(b) (i) What do you understand by the term cube? (2 marks)

(ii) In which crystal system does the cube belong? (1 mark)

(iii) Name any THREE crystal systems. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **cube** is a crystal form (a solid) bounded by **six equal square faces** that meet at right angles, with **12 equal edges** and **8 corners**. It is the form with **three equal crystallographic axes at $90^\circ$** to each other. Examples: halite, galena, fluorite, pyrite.

**(ii)** The cube belongs to the **cubic (isometric) system**.

**(iii)** Any three of: **cubic (isometric), tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, trigonal, monoclinic, triclinic**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe Galena and Orthoclase under the following physical properties;

(i) Colour. (2 marks)

(ii) Streak. (2 marks)

(iii) What is the hardness of diamond? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Colour:**

- **Galena:** lead-grey (silvery grey), with a bright metallic lustre.
- **Orthoclase:** usually **pink or flesh-coloured**, also white, cream or grey, with a glassy (vitreous) lustre.

**(ii) Streak:**

- **Galena:** **lead-grey (dark grey)** streak.
- **Orthoclase:** **white** (colourless) streak.

**(iii) Hardness of diamond:** **10** on Mohs' scale (the hardest mineral).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Describe basalt and granite under the following;

(i) Texture. (2 marks)

(ii) Mode of formation. Basalt (1 mark); Granite (1 mark)

(iii) Give the uses of granite. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Texture:**

- **Basalt:** **fine-grained (aphanitic)**; crystals too small to see without a lens; may be vesicular or porphyritic.
- **Granite:** **coarse-grained (phaneritic)**; interlocking crystals large enough to see with the naked eye.

**(ii) Mode of formation:**

- **Basalt:** an **extrusive (volcanic)** rock, formed when lava erupts at the surface and **cools quickly**.
- **Granite:** an **intrusive (plutonic)** rock, formed when magma **cools slowly deep in the crust** (in batholiths and stocks).

**(iii) Uses of granite** (any one or more): **building stone** and **monuments**, **kerbstones and paving**, **floor tiles and kitchen worktops**, and **crushed stone (aggregate)** for roads, concrete and railway ballast.
